reason: A validated Finding with a reproduced DISAGREE probe has no Recall-readable form: Recall selects only applied/approved Proposals, constraints, LearningNotes and MEMORY.md, so a later refactor that collapses a duplicated decision onto its owner (e.g. making ManagedAssetTargetCatalog the sync-path owner) is not shown the rule that the regression must target the branch the old gate never exercised. The same lesson was re-learned in later work, which adds the missing override-branch regression.
remaining_uncertainty: Single source Finding; recurrence is evidenced only by a later refactor applying the same rule, not by a second independent Finding.

Not shown that surfacing this row changes agent behaviour; MEMORY.md is already injected unconditionally and is about half of each briefing, so adding a row has a context cost that this Proposal does not measure.
new: When a decision implemented in several private copies is collapsed onto one owner, put the regression on the branch the old gate never exercised (for example an environment-variable override), not on the default branch where the copies already agreed.
boundary: Applies when collapsing duplicated decisions onto an owner. It does not require branch-level coverage of every code path.

The same lesson was re-learned in later work, which adds the missing override-branch regression.

validation_case.given: a decision implemented in several private copies, gated only through the default configuration
validation_case.when: the copies are collapsed onto one owner
validation_case.then: the regression that proves the collapse exercises the override branch where the copies disagreed, not only the default branch where they already matched
